title: A Compass for the Landfall
premise: Silas Thornbury, the only captain who can navigate the flooded upper reaches of the Kestrel River, is hired to resupply an expedition that has gone silent in the mountains. She finds one survivor — Dr. Imogen Vale, who discovered a pre-colonial compass artifact that her own sponsors will kill to control, and whose maps reveal a pass that closes with the first snows. Pursued by the expedition's armed backers and betrayed by the guide she trusted, Silas must choose between delivering the compass (and Imogen) to safety downriver or destroying it to end the greed it has awakened. In the final chapter she scuttles her beloved boat to block the pursuers at the narrows, crosses the pass on foot as the snows fall, and surrenders the broken compass to a museum — choosing love and identity over duty to any flag or fortune.
about_author: Hazel Coldharbour spent a decade working seasonal river runs before turning to writing full-time from a houseboat on the northern waterways. Her fiction is known for its granular knowledge of wild country and its stubborn, salt-crusted heroines.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Establishing life aboard the riverboat Magpie: her command of the sandbars, her debts, and her quiet loneliness after years alone on the water. A telegram arrives: the Harrow Expedition upriver has missed two check-ins, and the sponsors want her to run supplies and investigate. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a hunger for something more than cargo runs.

chapters.title: Dead Air at Kestrel Bend
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She pushes the Magpie into the flooded upper reaches no other captain will attempt, finding abandoned campsites and a wrecked radio mast. Signs suggest the expedition didn't die — they scattered deliberately. First glimpse of someone shadowing her boat through the trees. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; the wilderness begins to feel watchful.

chapters.title: What Vale Left Behind
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, shifting midway to Imogen Vale's journal entries. Silas finds the base camp burned by its own people and discovers Dr. Imogen Vale alive, half-starved, guarding a bronze compass that doesn't point north. Imogen explains: her sponsors want the artifact and the route it reveals, and she faked the silence to buy time. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who trust no one.

chapters.title: The Sponsors' Men
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The armed advance team led by Callum Reeve reaches the valley; Silas runs the rapids at night to slip past their picket, nearly losing the boat. They learn the compass points toward a high pass — the only crossing before snowfall — and that Reeve carries orders to retrieve it 'by any means.' Emotional beat: fear becoming anger; the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Portage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair abandons the Magpie at the last navigable pool and begins the overland portage with packs and a mule. Days of grueling travel build intimacy: Imogen's grief for her dead colleagues, Silas's stories of the river, the first unguarded laughter. Emotional beat: tenderness taking root where neither expected it.

chapters.title: The Guide's Bargain
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Their hired guide, Tomas, betrays them to Reeve for a pardon and passage home, stealing the compass overnight. Silas tracks him through cold rain and recovers it, but the confrontation costs them two days and most of their food. Emotional beat: bitter lesson that loyalty bought is loyalty sold; Silas questions whether anyone can be trusted, including herself.

chapters.title: North of the Treeline
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Above the treeline, storm-light and thin air strip both women bare. Imogen confesses the truth: the compass was never hers to find — she was planted on the expedition by a rival faction, and her 'rescue' of it was theft all along. Silas must decide whether the woman she's falling for is another kind of guide with a price. Emotional beat: identity laid open; love tested against deception.

chapters.title: Reeve's Ascent
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Reeve's party closes the gap, better provisioned and ruthless. A cat-and-mouse chase across a glacier field ends with Silas captured and the compass taken — but Reeve needs her pilot skills to get his men down the far side before the snows, so he keeps her alive. Imogen escapes into the whiteout. Emotional beat: despair, then the cold clarity of a captain reading weather others can't.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Climax. Alternating POV. Forced to pilot Reeve's men down the treacherous descent gorges, Silas reads the terrain like water and leads them onto unstable ground while Imogen doubles back through the storm. At the narrows, Silas triggers a rockslide that buries the pass behind them, stranding Reeve's party and burying the compass under a hundred tons of stone. Emotional beat: fury and sacrifice fused — she gives up the escape route, and nearly herself, to end the hunt.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Dual POV resolving into shared narration. Frostbitten but free, the two cross the last ridge as the first true snow falls and reach the coast settlement, where Silas reports everything — including her own role in the destruction — to an indifferent magistrate. Epilogue in spring: the Magpie raised and refitted, the two women running mail and passengers together, the compass a story told badly on purpose. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; identity chosen rather than assigned, love kept rather than traded.
